{{Short description|Generalization of a vector bundle}}
In algebraic geometry, a '''cone''' is a generalization of a [[vector bundle]]. Specifically, given a scheme ''X'', the [[relative Spec]]
:<math>C = \operatorname{Spec}_X R</math>
of a quasi-coherent graded [[sheaf of algebras|''O''<sub>''X''</sub>-algebra]] ''R'' is called the '''cone''' or '''affine cone''' of ''R''. Similarly, the [[relative Proj]]
:<math>\mathbb{P}(C) = \operatorname{Proj}_X R</math>
is called the '''projective cone''' of ''C'' or ''R''.

'''Note''': The cone comes with the <math>\mathbb{G}_m</math>-action due to the [[graded ring|grading]] of ''R''; this action is a part of the data of a cone (whence the terminology).<!-- Imprecise: maybe the quotient of the complement of the vertex? The projective cone of ''C'' is then the [[geometric invariant theory quotient]] of ''C'' with respect to the <math>\mathbb{G}_m</math>-action. -->

== Examples ==
*If ''X'' = Spec ''k'' is a point and ''R'' is a [[homogeneous coordinate ring]], then the affine cone of ''R'' is the (usual) [[Convex cone#Affine_convex_cones|affine cone]] over the [[projective variety]] corresponding to ''R''.
*If <math>R = \bigoplus_0^\infty I^n/I^{n+1}</math> for some [[ideal sheaf]] ''I'', then <math>\operatorname{Spec}_X R</math> is the [[normal cone]] to the closed scheme determined by ''I''.
*If <math>R = \bigoplus_0^\infty L^{\otimes n}</math> for some line bundle ''L'', then <math>\operatorname{Spec}_X R</math> is the total space of the dual of ''L''.
*More generally, given a vector bundle (finite-rank locally free sheaf) ''E'' on ''X'', if ''R''=Sym(''E''<sup>*</sup>) is the [[symmetric algebra]] generated by the dual of ''E'', then the cone <math>\operatorname{Spec}_X R</math> is the total space of ''E'', often written just as ''E'', and the projective cone <math>\operatorname{Proj}_X R</math> is the [[projective bundle]] of ''E'', which is written as <math>\mathbb{P}(E)</math>.
*Let <math>\mathcal{F}</math> be a coherent [[sheaf on an algebraic stack|sheaf]] on a [[Deligne–Mumford stack]] ''X''. Then let <math>C(\mathcal{F}) := \operatorname{Spec}_X(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal{F})).</math><ref>{{harvnb|Behrend|Fantechi|1997|loc=§ 1.}}</ref> For any <math>f: T \to X</math>, since global Spec is a right adjoint to the direct image functor, we have: <math>C(\mathcal{F})(T) = \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal{F}), f_* \mathcal{O}_T)</math>; in particular, <math>C(\mathcal{F})</math> is a commutative [[group scheme]] over ''X''.
*Let ''R'' be a graded <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-algebra such that <math>R_0 = \mathcal{O}_X</math> and <math>R_1</math> is coherent and locally generates ''R'' as <math>R_0</math>-algebra. Then there is a [[closed immersion]]
::<math>\operatorname{Spec}_X R \hookrightarrow C(R_1)</math>
:given by <math>\operatorname{Sym}(R_1) \to R</math>. Because of this, <math>C(R_1)</math> is called the abelian hull of the cone <math>\operatorname{Spec}_X R.</math> For example, if <math>R = \oplus_0^{\infty} I^n/I^{n+1}</math> for some ideal sheaf ''I'', then this embedding is the embedding of the normal cone into the normal bundle.

=== Computations ===
Consider the complete intersection ideal <math>(f,g_1,g_2,g_3) \subset \mathbb{C}[x_0,\ldots,x_n]</math> and let <math>X</math> be the projective scheme defined by the ideal sheaf <math>\mathcal{I} = (f)(g_1,g_2,g_3)</math>. Then, we have the isomorphism of <math>\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^n}</math>-algebras given by{{citation needed|date=August 2019}}
:<math>
\bigoplus_{n\geq 0 } \frac{\mathcal{I}^n}{\mathcal{I}^{n+1}} \cong \frac{\mathcal{O}_X[a,b,c]}{(g_2a - g_1b, g_3a - g_1c, g_3b - g_2c)}
</math>

== Properties ==
If <math>S \to R</math> is a graded homomorphism of graded ''O''<sub>''X''</sub>-algebras, then one gets an induced morphism between the cones:
:<math>C_R = \operatorname{Spec}_X R \to C_S = \operatorname{Spec}_X S</math>.
If the homomorphism is surjective, then one gets closed immersions <math>C_R \hookrightarrow C_S,\, \mathbb{P}(C_R) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}(C_S).</math>

In particular, assuming ''R''<sub>0</sub> = ''O''<sub>''X''</sub>, the construction applies to the projection <math>R = R_0 \oplus R_1 \oplus \cdots \to R_0</math> (which is an [[augmentation map]]) and gives
:<math>\sigma: X \hookrightarrow C_R</math>.
It is a section; i.e., <math>X \overset{\sigma}\to C_R \to X</math> is the identity and is called the zero-section embedding.

Consider the graded algebra ''R''[''t''] with variable ''t'' having degree one: explicitly, the ''n''-th degree piece is
:<math>R_n \oplus R_{n-1} t \oplus R_{n-2} t^2 \oplus \cdots \oplus R_0 t^n</math>.
Then the affine cone of it is denoted by <math>C_{R[t]} = C_R \oplus 1</math>. The projective cone <math>\mathbb{P}(C_R \oplus 1)</math> is called the '''projective completion''' of ''C''<sub>''R''</sub>. Indeed, the zero-locus ''t''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0 is exactly <math>\mathbb{P}(C_R)</math> and the complement is the open subscheme ''C''<sub>''R''</sub>. The locus ''t''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0 is called the hyperplane at infinity.

== ''O''(1) ==
Let ''R'' be a quasi-coherent graded ''O''<sub>''X''</sub>-algebra such that ''R''<sub>0</sub> = ''O''<sub>''X''</sub> and ''R'' is locally generated as ''O''<sub>''X''</sub>-algebra by ''R''<sub>1</sub>. Then, by definition, the projective cone of ''R'' is:
:<math>\mathbb{P}(C) = \operatorname{Proj}_X R = \varinjlim \operatorname{Proj}(R(U))</math>
where the [[direct limit|colimit]] runs over open affine subsets ''U'' of ''X''. By assumption ''R''(''U'') has finitely many degree-one generators ''x''<sub>''i''</sub>'s. Thus,
:<math>\operatorname{Proj}(R(U)) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^r \times U.</math>
Then <math>\operatorname{Proj}(R(U))</math> has the line bundle ''O''(1) given by the [[hyperplane bundle]] <math>\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^r}(1)</math> of <math>\mathbb{P}^r</math>; gluing such local ''O''(1)'s, which agree locally, gives the line bundle ''O''(1) on <math>\mathbb{P}(C)</math>.

For any integer ''n'', one also writes ''O''(''n'') for the ''n''-th tensor power of ''O''(1). If the cone ''C''=Spec<sub>''X''</sub>''R'' is the total space of a vector bundle ''E'', then ''O''(-1) is the [[tautological line bundle]] on the [[projective bundle]] '''P'''(''E'').

'''Remark''': When the (local) generators of ''R'' have degree other than one, the construction of ''O''(1) still goes through but with a [[weighted projective space]] in place of a projective space; so the resulting ''O''(1) is not necessarily a line bundle. In the language of [[divisor (algebraic geometry)|divisor]], this ''O''(1) corresponds to a '''Q'''-Cartier divisor.
